raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: Are you there?
ParticipantB: Yes, I am. How can I help you?
ParticipantA: I need to talk about kids. Do you have any children?
ParticipantB: No, I don't have any children yet. Why do you ask?
ParticipantA: Me neither. But I was thinking about it. Do you think having kids is good?
ParticipantB: That's a big question. I think it depends on what you want in life.
ParticipantA: Yeah, I guess so. My mom says it's the best thing in the world.
ParticipantB: Some people feel that way. Others say it changes everything in a hard way.
ParticipantA: How old do you have to be to have kids? Like, is there an age limit?
ParticipantB: Not really a legal limit for everyone, but usually people wait until they are older, like twenty-five or thirty.
ParticipantA: I am thirty-seven. Is that too old?
ParticipantB: No, thirty-seven is fine. Many people have kids at your age.
ParticipantA: Really? That makes me feel better. I thought people had to be younger.
ParticipantB: Biology says it gets harder as you get older, but it definitely happens all the time.
ParticipantA: What about money? Can you afford kids at thirty-seven?
ParticipantB: It is expensive. You need a stable job and a savings plan.
ParticipantA: I have a job. I just finished high school last year. Can I afford it then?
ParticipantB: That might be difficult at first. You might need to save for a while before starting a family.
ParticipantA: Oh, that sounds scary. I don't have much money right now.
ParticipantB: That is a real concern. You could start small, like fostering a pet or getting an apartment with a roommate.
ParticipantA: A pet? That sounds kind of like a kid. Would that count?
ParticipantB: It's not exactly a child, but it teaches responsibility. That is a good first step.
ParticipantA: Maybe I should get a dog first. Then I can learn how to take care of someone.
ParticipantB: That is a great idea. It gives you experience without the full cost of a baby.
ParticipantA: But what if I want a real baby? Do I need to go back to school?
ParticipantB: Many parents with degrees have kids. It helps to understand how to teach them.
ParticipantA: I only have a high school diploma. Do you think that stops me from being a good mom?
ParticipantB: No, it does not stop you. Education helps, but love and patience matter more.
ParticipantA: That makes me happy to hear. What if I go to college later?
ParticipantB: You can do that. Many people return to school while their kids are in school too.
ParticipantA: That would be hard though. Balancing work, school, and kids sounds crazy.
ParticipantB: It is very hard. You need support from a partner or family to make it work.
ParticipantA: I don't have a partner. Is it possible to raise kids alone at thirty-seven?
ParticipantB: It is possible, but it is very challenging. You need a strong support network and a lot of planning.
ParticipantA: Maybe I should find someone to help me first?
ParticipantB: Yes, building a life with someone can share the burden. Are you seeing anyone?
ParticipantA: Not really. I just meet people sometimes, but we don't talk about kids much.
ParticipantB: Maybe you should bring it up next time. It is an important life topic.
ParticipantA: I will try that. Do you think I should live in a bigger city where people help each other?
ParticipantB: Cities can be good because there are communities and resources for families.
ParticipantA: My town is small. There are not many people here to help.
ParticipantB: If you move, you need to find a place with good schools and support groups.
ParticipantA: Moving sounds expensive. Can I just stay here and save up?
ParticipantB: You could stay here. It depends on your budget and your goals.
ParticipantA: I want to save for my future. Do you think kids ruin your dreams?
ParticipantB: It changes your dreams. You focus on providing for them instead of just yourself.
ParticipantA: I like my freedom. I want to travel and buy my own house soon.
ParticipantB: You can do that before having kids, but once you have them, your priorities change quickly.
ParticipantA: That is true. I don't know if I want to give up my freedom.
ParticipantB: Some parents say they don't miss their freedom much. They find joy in their kids.
ParticipantA: Maybe I will wait five years to see how I feel.
ParticipantB: Taking your time is wise. You should not rush into it if you are unsure.
ParticipantA: Thank you for talking to me. You gave me a lot to think about.
ParticipantB: You are welcome. It was good discussing this with someone your age.
ParticipantA: It was nice talking to you too. Have a good day.
ParticipantB: You too. Bye.
ParticipantA: Bye.
